extracted.intended_audience: distance/online education administrators, student-support staff, instructional designers, and faculty involved in providing learner supports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for designing and delivering non-academic supports for online and distance learners (prospective, current, and alumni), including administrative, technological, metacognitive, counselling, community, library, governance, and disability-specific services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall goal of learner supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports should develop learner independence and facilitate the learning process by being flexible, accessible, and readily available when needed; the overall goal is a learner-support-services system “where students feel at home, where they feel valued, and which they find manageable” (Tait, 2000, p. 289).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports should show clear value to learners (otherwise they won't use them) and be available but not intrusive; plan a 'constellation' of supports across administrative, technological, academic, and social areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess prospective learner readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask about readiness for online learning (academic, financial, family/time), language proficiency, computing/connectivity access, mathematics readiness, program-specific skills, and career/educational goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide self-assessment tools (e.g., 'Am I Ready' resources), follow-up email counselling, and direct learners to remedial or preparatory resources and program-specific tutorials as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum computer and connectivity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear information so potential learners can determine if they have (or have access to) necessary hardware, software, and connectivity to study online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer short sample experiences or toolkits that illustrate expectations (e.g., Learning Toolkit), describe options for offline/print access (CD-ROM, printed materials), and state any alternative arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-planning and program advising
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide online resources that help learners determine interests/skills and align career maps with programs; offer program advising that helps plan programs, account for transfer credit, and adapt to changes in goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage initial exploration by the learner, then offer advisor refinement (email/telephone). Advisors should be readily available and have access to program and transfer information to accommodate changes over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and logistic service standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative processes (e.g., course registration, exam requests, grade reporting) must be smooth, flexible, and give learners control; service standards (response times, turnaround for grades, email replies, library requests) should be clear and readily available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make benchmarks public so students know expectations and service units have targets (e.g., how long to receive registration confirmation or assignment feedback). Consider challenges of dual-mode institutions and continuous vs. term-based enrolment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course materials distribution options
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multiple delivery methods for course materials (online content, printed versions, CD-ROMs, commercial online booksellers, institutional distribution) to accommodate learner preferences and bandwidth constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider warehousing, inventory, distribution costs; offer electronic versions and publisher-supplemented online resources; make printed or offline formats available on demand (possibly for additional charge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and technological support formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Use coordinated support structures such as an information centre (institutional/program information), a computing helpdesk (technical troubleshooting), and a call centre (program-specific questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these services work together and that attendants have access to critical databases/expertise to resolve issues or escalate appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of effective tech/info support
rubrics_metrics.description: Support units should have reliable networks; asynchronous access (e.g., email) with '24/7' availability; synchronous access (e.g., toll-free telephone) at identified times; quick response with acknowledgement and follow-up; and follow-through to resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provide simple, clear instructions; access by staff to all critical information; and the ability to identify systemic problems in policies or systems and suggest changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portal integration and single access
rubrics_metrics.description: Use portals to individualize and integrate online interactions, reducing multiple sign-ons and dispersed websites, to make access easier and more efficient for learners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portals should centralize course access and web-based functions and simplify user workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacognitive supports (learning how to learn online)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide resources that teach 'learning how to learn' online: time management, study schedules, balancing life demands, reducing exam anxiety, strategies for becoming a successful online learner, and supports for writing and research skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer web-based exercises and tutorials, online strategies for exam anxiety, and tools that build learner confidence and self-regulation; adopt constructivist approaches to foster active, self-directed learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing resources and formative feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide online writing instruction and services (e.g., Paradigm Online Writing Assistant, institutional 'Write Site') that allow students to submit drafts and receive feedback on organization, mechanics, grammar, and style before formal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make writing help widely available as part of metacognitive supports to strengthen assignment performance and academic communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual-property and plagiarism education
rubrics_metrics.description: Make intellectual honesty expectations readily available; provide reminders in assignment directions, links to approved style guides, links to anti-plagiarism services (e.g., Turnitin), and online tutorials on correct attribution and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer exercises and tutorials to teach plagiarism concepts and avoidance; recognize cultural differences in IP understanding and ensure frequent reinforcement of expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-building and peer-support tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster communities of practice using asynchronous conferences, text-based chat, synchronous audio conferencing, blogs, wikis, and social software to support interaction, peer assistance, and a sense of belonging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide moderated in-course forums and opportunities for informal, cross-course interactions (meet-and-greet areas, study-buddy matching, mentoring); consider resource-constrained contexts (supporting self-directed groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Library services focused on access and research support
rubrics_metrics.description: Shift library focus from holdings to access; integrate library services into courses, provide web-based instruction on searching online databases, conducting literature reviews, and facilitating student research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure library resources and training are available for undergraduate and postgraduate needs, and provide assistance in using digital libraries effectively in assignments and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online educational counselling roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselling in online environments should include: (1) developing online resources to identify/address barriers, (2) interacting with learners when intervention is required, and (3) working with institutional staff to ensure processes support learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep personal counselling limited to immediate crisis resolution and referral; counsellors should know local community resources for referrals and be trained to identify learners who would benefit from counselling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student rights, codes of conduct, and ombuds services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clearly articulated student rights and responsibilities (code of conduct) and a highly visible ombuds office to assist learners who do not know where to turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ombuds can also identify institutional policy and procedure problems; make rights and conduct information available online and in print on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional governance and student union engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include student representatives in governance (boards, senior committees) and support student unions (networks, single institutional contacts, fee collection assistance) to ensure student perspectives inform decisions and to foster student belonging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use electronic meeting methods to maximize participation, keep unions apprised of institutional issues, engage in shared initiatives, and demonstrate appreciation for union work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni resources and post-graduation engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide alumni sections on institutional websites and opportunities for ongoing contact, fundraising, and planned giving to maintain engagement after graduation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alumni as part of the broader learner community and offer communication and involvement pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability-specific supports and accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide individualized disability services that may include information, assessment of academic/technological accommodations, educational and career counselling, referrals, program planning, time-management assistance, progress monitoring, registration help, funding assistance, alternate-format materials, tutoring/strategists/interpreting/reader/scribe, exam accommodations, course time extensions, advocacy, liaison with departments, and volunteer assistance (note taking, exam-writing help, mobility assistance, tape readings, library research help, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a proactive approach by planning disability-specific supports prior to enrolment; not all students will need all services but readiness and individual assessment are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and monitor disability-service uptake
rubrics_metrics.description: Track numbers of prospective and active students receiving disability services to plan resources appropriately (e.g., Athabasca University growth statistics as an example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such data to justify services, forecast demand, and adjust supports over time.
